forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif confirmed June 12 agreement on final MOU text via Pakistan-hosted facilitated sessions; VP Vance confirmed June 14 digital signing by named US (Witkoff) and Iranian representatives through Islamabad mediation — both before EOD June 16 horizon. Iran participated actively in producing the MOU text, constituting a held facilitated session (not mere written-message relay). June 17 presidential signing (Pezeshkian in Tehran, Trump at Versailles) confirmed by Al Jazeera, NPR, CBS.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

Strait remained physically obstructed by ~80 Iranian mines (Maham-3 and Maham-7 types); demining active but not complete; AIS spoofing/dark vessels complicate upward counts. 50/day 7-day-average threshold not achieved.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: Sunday cold-start audit: p_inherited=0.35, p_cold=0.72 (gap=37pp; 47-day staleness since May 19 last_reasoned_at). Judge selects 0.72. Three compounding developments: (1) coalition at 60 seats following Yuli Edelstein's Likud departure July 2 to form Edelstein-Shaked alliance — below the 61-seat majority threshold in the 120-seat Knesset; (2) Knesset legal adviser formally recommended July 17 dissolution; (3) Hamas explicitly cited Israeli elections as reason to delay Gaza reconstruction talks, confirming external actors treat early dissolution as base case. Prior p=0.35 from May 11 is methodologically invalid at 47 days. Resolution requires a formal Knesset roll-call vote confirming majority loss or dissolution bill passage through second/third readings — no such formal vote has yet occurred; ACTIVE status maintained.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (fewer than 61 seats in a documented vote) OR if the Knesset passes a dissolution bill on second and third readings scheduling early elections, confirmed by official Knesset record or TIER1 source, before EOD 2026-10-27. Netanyahu remaining as caretaker PM after dissolution does not block YES resolution.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 seats but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: RESOLVE-YES. If Netanyahu resigns without formal Knesset majority vote, RESOLVE-YES if confirmed by TIER1. If elections are held and Netanyahu wins with a new coalition, RESOLVE-YES (original coalition collapsed). If no dissolution or majority vote by Oct 27, RESOLVE-NO. Reviewed weekly (Sundays); intra-week updates only for formal vote or major documented coalition departure.

forecasts.question: Will a 7-day rolling average of >=50 commercial transits/day through the Strait of Hormuz be recorded in IMF PortWatch or equivalent AIS-based data before EOD 2026-08-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast; successor to RESOLVED-NO F4. Current 7-day MA ~13-27 transits/day (June 21-July 2 PortWatch range); single-day count of 39 on July 3 — highest post-war figure but below threshold. Pre-war baseline ~84/day. Demining active (CENTCOM confirmed) but ~80 mines remain and clearing is slow. The 60-day MOU window (through ~Aug 16) provides diplomatic cover for free passage but not physical clearance. Iran's July 4 fee declaration creates commercial uncertainty for the post-August 16 period. Reaching 50/day by Aug 15 requires roughly 4x acceleration in 41 days — possible if demining clears the inbound lane by late July but not the base case.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch Strait of Hormuz 7-day moving average equals or exceeds 50 commercial transits/day for any 7-day window ending on or before 2026-08-15. Naval-escorted convoys count as commercial transits if the escorted vessels are commercial-flagged. Military-only movements do not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Primary: IMF PortWatch (portwatch.imf.org) official data. Secondary: Windward AIS, Lloyd's List, NBC News Hormuz tracker. If PortWatch shows >=50 and AIS-dark vessels suspected of inflating counts, apply 15% haircut; if adjusted count still >=50, resolve YES.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If data gap exceeds 5 days in PortWatch during the window, use Windward or Lloyd's as substitute. If all sources show AIS-dark rates >30% (spoofing context), AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.
